text:
alex_m: CI turned red on main after the toolchain image roll (today morning). failing on a bunch of C++ link errors, looks like libstdc++ ABI mismatch. filing here before I start bisecting.
ci-bot: Build failed: //cc:server (linux-x86_64) — https://ci.internal/reports/1968456789 — commit 7f3a2b1
alex_m: failing error snippet:
```
/opt/gcc/lib64/libstdc++.so.6: undefined reference to `_ZNSs6appendEPKc'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

alex_m: repro locally with:
```
bazel test //cc/... --config=linux_x86_64 --test_output=errors
```

maria_g: ugh. Did the docker toolchain image bump the distro or gcc version? Any link to the image diff?

alex_m: pinging eng-infra infra-team in the image PR — but quick note: previous green was commit 7f2c9d. 7f3a2b1 is the one that rolled the image. I can try a bisect if folks prefer.

chen_w: I can spare time to bisect. Quick question: are the symbols missing at link time or undefined at runtime? looks linker-level from the snippet.

alex_m: linker-level. lots of undefined refs to std::string symbols.

jonah: try setting -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0 as a quick experiment? if the new image switched libstdc++ ABI, that could explain it.

alex_m: good call — trying that now. patch:
```diff
- copts: ["-O2"]
+ copts: ["-O2", "-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0"]
```

alex_m: quick local run with that made the binary link past the previous error, but we need a proper root cause (compatibility between prebuilt deps and new libstdc++)

maria_g: if prebuilt artifacts were compiled with the old ABI, linking against a new libstdc++ could break. Are we pulling any system-installed libs from the image or using hermetic builds?

alex_m: we link some prebuilt third_party .a files (packaged in artifacts/) that are not rebuilt every roll. looks like they were built with old ABI.

chen_w: OK. two options:
- rebuild those prebuilts with the new toolchain (slow)
- provide a transitional image that still has the older libstdc++ for now

jonah: also can we change our toolchain config so Bazel uses the distro's gcc/libstdc++ consistent with how those prebuilts were built? Might be messy.

alex_m: filing a short incident note and will open a PR with the temporary copts change to unblock CI for the release branch. Long term we'll schedule prebuilts rebuild.

maria_g: For bisecting: if you want help, run: `git bisect start --term-old=green 7f2c9d --term-new=bad 7f3a2b1` and run the bazel test script per-commit. I can run halves if you hit flakey CI.

alex_m: thanks — starting bisect now. tagging @chen_w for assistance if I get stuck.

ci-bot: Rerun requested by alex_m — queued: https://ci.internal/rebuild/1968456799

chen_w: if you want me to take over the bisect, I can fork your branch and run in a controlled VM with the image pinned.

alex_m: appreciated. I'll push my bisect script to the repo under tools/ci/bisect.sh and share the link in a follow-up.

jonah: also, add a note to the release-channel channels to avoid promoting that image until prebuilts are rebuilt. :warning:

alex_m: will do. short-term plan:
- push copts workaround to unblock CI
- coordinate prebuilts rebuild and/or image rollback
- finish bisect to confirm exact offending change

maria_g: sounds good. keep us posted here with the bisect commit hash that introduced the break so we can trace what changed in the image.

alex_m: will update in this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
